The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, may His praise be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue. Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing.﴾ (58:1)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Allah has indeed heard﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾. She who was pleading with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning her husband was a woman from the Ansar.

The people of knowledge differed about her lineage and her name. Some of them said: Khawla bint Tha'laba. Some of them said: her name is Khuwayla bint Tha'laba.

Others said: she is Khuwayla bint Khuwaylid.

Others said: she is Khuwayla bint al-Samit.

Others said: she is Khuwayla daughter of al-Dulaj. Her pleading with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerned her husband, whose name was Aws ibn al-Samit, her returning to him about his matter, and what he had said to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother," and her dialogue with him about that. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) held this view, and the transmission (riwaya) supports it.

Mention of those who said this, and the reports narrated about it:

◆ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-Aliya say: "Khuwayla daughter of al-Dulaj came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while A'isha was washing one side of his head. She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my companionship with my husband has lasted long, I have borne him children, and he has likened me to his mother's back.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'You have become unlawful to him.' She said: 'I complain to Allah of my destitution.' Then she said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my companionship has lasted long, and I have borne him children.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'You have become unlawful to him.' Whenever he said to her, 'You have become unlawful to him,' she cried out and said: 'I complain to Allah of my destitution.' He said: Then revelation descended, while A'isha was still washing the other side of his head. A'isha gestured to her to be silent. She said: When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it would seize him like a deep sleep. When the revelation ended, he said: 'Call your husband.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to him: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿And those who liken their wives to their mothers' backs and then retract what they said﴾, meaning return to it, ﴿then [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another.﴾ [He asked]: 'Can you find a slave?' He said: 'No.' He said: ﴿And whoever cannot [find one], then [the penalty is] fasting two months consecutively﴾. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if I do not eat three times a day, my sight dims.' He said: ﴿And whoever is unable, then [the penalty is] feeding sixty needy persons.﴾ He said: 'Can you feed sixty needy persons?' He said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, unless you help me.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helped him, and he fed them."

◆ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "It was mentioned to us that Khuwayla daughter of Tha'laba, whose husband Aws ibn al-Samit had likened her to his mother's back, came complaining to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She said: 'My husband has likened me, now that my age has grown and my bones have grown weak.' So Allah revealed concerning her what you hear: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾, and he recited until He reached ﴿Indeed, He is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who liken their wives to their mothers' backs and then retract what they said﴾, meaning he wanted to have intercourse after his saying that. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him and said to him: 'Can you free a slave?' He said: 'I have no means for that,' or he said: 'I do not find [one].' He said: 'Can you fast two months consecutively?' He said: 'No, by Allah; if he misses his meal every day several times, his sight is dimmed.' He said: 'Can you feed sixty needy persons?' He said: 'No, by Allah, unless you help me with some aid and blessing (du'a).'"

Bishr said, Yazid said: "He means supplication (du'a)." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helped him with fifteen sa's, and Allah united his affair, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

◆ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾. He said: "That was Aws ibn al-Samit, who likened his wife Khuwayla daughter of Tha'laba. She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my age has grown, my bones have weakened, and my husband has likened me.' So Allah revealed: ﴿And those who liken their wives to their mothers' backs﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿then retract what they said﴾, meaning he wanted to have intercourse after His words: ﴿then [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another.﴾ The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him to himself and said: 'Can you free a slave?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Can you fast two months consecutively?' He said: 'If he misses his meal three times a day, his sight dims.' He said: 'Can you feed sixty needy persons?' He said: 'No, unless the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helps me with aid and blessing.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helped him with fifteen sa's, and Allah united his affair, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A man, in the Jahiliyya, when he said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' she became forbidden to him in Islam. The first person to make this declaration (zihar) in Islam was Aws ibn al-Samit. He had a paternal cousin as his wife, called Khuwayla bint Khuwaylid, and he likened her. He was distressed and said: 'I see you have become forbidden to me.' She said to him the same. He said: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' She came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and found with him a woman who was dressing his hair. She informed him, and he said: 'O Khuwayla, we have not been commanded anything regarding your matter.' Then Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'O Khuwayla, rejoice!' She said: 'Good news!' He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to her: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿then [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another.﴾ She said: 'What slave do we have? By Allah, he has no slave except me.' He said: ﴿And whoever cannot [find one], then [the penalty is] fasting two months consecutively﴾. She said: 'By Allah, if he did not drink three times a day, his sight would be lost.' He said: ﴿And whoever is unable, then [the penalty is] feeding sixty needy persons﴾. She said: 'From where? There is nothing but one meal until another [meal].' He said: So he helped him with half a wasq, thirty sa's, and a wasq is sixty sa's. He said: 'Let him feed sixty needy persons, and let him return to you.'"

◆ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿then [the penalty is] feeding sixty needy persons﴾. This was because Khawla bint al-Samit, a woman from the Ansar, was likened by her husband, who said: 'You are to me like the back of my mother.' She came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My husband married me, and I was the most beloved of people to him. Then, when I grew old and advanced in years, he said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he left me to no one else. If you know of any concession for me, O Messenger of Allah, by which you would relieve me and him, then inform me of it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded anything regarding your matter until now, but return to your house. If I am commanded anything, I will not keep it from you, if Allah wills." So she returned to her house, and Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) in the Book the concession for her and for her husband: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾ The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for her husband. When he came to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What did you intend by the oath you swore?" He said: "Is there an expiation for it?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Can you free a slave?" He said: "Then my entire wealth would be lost. The slave is expensive, and I have little wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Can you then fast two months consecutively?" He said: "No, by Allah; if I did not eat three times a day, my sight would be dimmed." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Can you feed sixty needy persons?" He said: "No, by Allah, unless you help me in that with aid and blessing." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, I will help you with fifteen sa's, and I pray for blessing for you," and the matter between them was settled.

He said: And [Allah] made in it the freeing of a slave for one who is well-off; no expiation is accepted except the freeing of a slave if he is well-off, before they touch one another. If he is not well-off, then [the penalty is] fasting two months consecutively; fasting is not permitted for him except if he is in difficulty, unless he is unable, and if he is unable, then feeding sixty needy persons. All of this is before intercourse.

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar al-Madani, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "Khawla bint Tha'laba was under Aws ibn al-Samit, and he was a man afflicted with madness (lamam). In one of his periods of estrangement from her [[al-Hijra, with a kasra on the ha', is the name for the verb hajr, which is to cut off from one's wife]], he said: 'You are to me like the back of my mother.' Then he regretted what he had said, and said to her: 'I do not think you are anything but forbidden to me.' She said: 'Do not say that. By Allah, Allah does not love divorce.' She said: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him.' He said: 'I find myself too shy to ask him about this.' She said: 'Then let me ask him.' He said to her: 'Ask him.' So she went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, Aws ibn al-Samit is the father of my children and the most beloved of people to me. He has said a word, and by the One who revealed the Book to you, he did not mention divorce. He said: "You are to me like the back of my mother."' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I do not see you as anything but having become forbidden to him.' She said: 'Do not say that, O Prophet of Allah. By Allah, he did not mention divorce.' She repeatedly returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) [with her plea], then said: 'O Allah, I complain to You today of the severity of my condition, my loneliness, and what is hard for me of his separation. O Allah, send down [a ruling] upon the tongue of Your Prophet.' She did not move from her place until Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾, up to where He mentioned the expiations. The Prophet (ﷺ) summoned him and said: 'Free a slave.' He said: 'I do not find one.' He said: 'Fast two months consecutively.' He said: 'I cannot, for I fast one day and it is hard for me.' He said: 'Feed sixty needy persons.' He said: 'As for this, yes.'"

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, concerning His words: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾. He said: "It was revealed concerning a woman named Khawla." Ikrima said: "Her name was Khuwayla bint Tha'laba. Her husband Aws ibn al-Samit had made her like his mother's back. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Her husband has made her, as far as he is concerned, like the back of his mother.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I do not see you as anything but having become forbidden to him.' At that time he was washing his head. She said: 'Look, may I be ransomed for you, O Prophet of Allah.' He said: 'I do not see you as anything but having become forbidden to him.' She said: 'Look into my case, O Messenger of Allah.' She continued to argue with him. Then he turned his head to be washed, and she moved to the other side, saying: 'Look, may Allah make me your ransom, O Prophet of Allah.' The washerwoman said: 'Cut short your talk and your addressing him, O Khuwayla. Do you not see the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) becoming troubled, as he is about to receive revelation?' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾ ... until He reached: ﴿then retract what they said﴾. Qatada said: 'He has made her forbidden, then he wants to return to her and have intercourse with her.' ﴿Then [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave﴾ ... until He reached: ﴿Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ Ayyub said: 'I think he mentioned it from Ikrima, that a man said: "O Prophet of Allah, I do not find a slave." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will not add to your burden." So Allah revealed to him: ﴿Then fasting two months consecutively before they touch one another﴾. He said: 'By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I cannot bear fasting. If I do not eat so-and-so many meals in a day, I suffer and suffer.' He began to complain to him. He said: 'I will not add to your burden.' Then it was revealed: ﴿And whoever is unable, then [the penalty is] feeding sixty needy persons.﴾"

◆ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿She who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾. He said: "She pleads with Muhammad (ﷺ), and she complains to Allah about his old age and her old age, until his soul and her womb were shaken."

◆ al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's words: ﴿She who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾. He said: "[She pleads] with Muhammad about her husband, who had likened her, and she complains to Allah." Then he mentioned the rest of the report similarly.

◆ 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Aban al-'Attar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated to us, from 'Urwa, that he wrote to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan: "You wrote to me asking me about Khuwayla daughter of Aws ibn al-Samit. She is not the daughter of Aws ibn al-Samit, but she is the wife of Aws. Aws was a man afflicted with madness (lamam), and when his madness became severe, he would liken her, and when his madness left him, he would not say anything of that. She came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeking a ruling and complaining to Allah. So Allah revealed what you have heard, and that was their affair."

◆ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrate, from Ma'mar ibn 'Abd Allah, from Yusuf ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, who said: Khuwayla, the wife of Aws ibn al-Samit, told me: "There was something between me and him, meaning her husband. He said: 'You are to me like the back of my mother.' Then he went out to the assembly of his people, then returned and sought to have intercourse with me. I said: 'No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, until my affair and yours reaches the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who will decide about me and you.' He was an old man, weak, and I overcame him with what a strong woman overcomes a weak man with. Then I went out to a neighbor of mine and borrowed her clothes, and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and sat before him, and I told him about his matter. I had not moved before revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then she said: 'He cannot do that.' He said: 'We will help him with that by a measure of dates.' I said: 'And I will help him with another measure, and he will feed sixty needy persons.'"

◆ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Tamim, from 'Urwa, from A'isha, who said: "Praise be to Allah, who has made His hearing encompass voices. The woman who pleads [Khawla] came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while I was in a corner of the house, complaining about her husband, and I could not hear what she was saying. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

◆ 'Isa ibn 'Uthman al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Tamim ibn Salama, from 'Urwa, from A'isha, who said: "Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all voices. The woman would converse with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I would hear some of her speech, while some of her speech was hidden from me, when Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾."

◆ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Tamim ibn Salama, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, who said: A'isha said: "Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses everything. I would hear the speech of Khawla bint Tha'laba, and some of it would be hidden from me, while she was complaining about her husband to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, he consumed my youth, and I bore him children. When my age grew old and my children stopped, he likened me. O Allah, I complain to You.'" He said: "She had not moved before Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with these verses: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾." He said: "Her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit."

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Tamīm ibn Salama, from 'Urwa, from 'Ā'isha, who said: "Praise be to Allah, who has encompassed all voices in His hearing. Indeed, Khawla was complaining to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about her husband, and some of what she said was sometimes hidden from me." She said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾.

⁕ al-Rabī' ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Hammād ibn Salama narrated to us, from Hishām ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'Ā'isha, that Jamīla was the wife of Aws ibn al-Sāmit, and he had a form of madness (lamam), and when his madness became severe he would declare (ẓāhara) his wife unlawful to himself. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of ẓihār (the pre-Islamic practice of declaring one's wife unlawful by likening her to one's mother's back).

⁕ Yaḥyā ibn Bishr al-Qarqasānī narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Azīz ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: Khaṣīf narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn 'Abbās, who said: "The ẓihār of the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam) was a divorce. The first person to declare his wife unlawful in Islam was Aws ibn al-Sāmit, the brother of 'Ubāda ibn al-Sāmit, from his wife of the Khazraj, who was Khawla bint Tha'laba ibn Mālik. When he declared her unlawful, she thought that this would be a divorce, so she came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Aws has declared me unlawful to himself, and if we separate we will be ruined. I have borne children by him, and I have been with him for a long time.' She complained of this and wept, and nothing had yet come down concerning it. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then called him and said: 'Can you free a slave?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I cannot.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered [provision] for him until he freed one on his behalf, and then he returned to his family."

It is mentioned that this (wording) is in the recitation (qirā'a) of 'Abd Allāh ibn Mas'ūd: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who argues with you concerning her husband﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and complains to Allah﴾,
meaning: the one who pleads complains to Allah of the distress she has because of her husband's ẓihār against her, and asks Him for relief. ﴿And Allah hears your exchange﴾, meaning: the exchange between you and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the one pleading is Khawla bint Tha'laba. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah hears what they respond to and discuss with each other, and the other speech of His creatures, and He sees what they do and what all His servants do.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 2:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Those of you who divorce [by zihar] their wives, [saying to them, "You are] not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who bore them. And indeed, they say an objectionable word and a falsehood. And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Those who forbid their wives to themselves by making the back of their mothers forbidden to them, so they say to them, "You are to us like the backs of our mothers." This was the divorce of a man from his wife in the Jahiliyyah (the Time of Ignorance, the pre-Islamic period).

Thus Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: "Zihar was a divorce in the Jahiliyyah, whereby if one of them uttered it, he would never return to his wife. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning it what He revealed."

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah, except Nafi', and the majority of the reciters of Kufah, except Asim, recited it: ﴿yuzzahiruna﴾ with a fatha on the yaʼ, a shaddah on the zay, and an alif, and they recited the other similarly in the sense of yatazahharun (they make zihar with one another), then the taʼ was assimilated into the zay so that the two became a single shaddah zay. It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is ﴿yatazahharuna﴾, and that is a confirmation and strengthening of this recitation. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr recited it likewise with a fatha on the yaʼ and a shaddah on the zay, except that they recited it without an alif: ﴿yuzzahhirna﴾. Asim recited it ﴿yuzahiruna﴾ with a light zay, a damma on the yaʼ, and an alif.

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that all these recitations are close in meaning. As for ﴿yazzahharuna﴾, it is from tazahara, so he yatazahharu; as for ﴿yazzahharuna﴾, it is from tazahhara, so he yatazahharu, then the taʼ was assimilated into the zay, so it is said yazhar. As for ﴿yuzahiruna﴾, it is from zahara, yuzahiru. So whichever of these three recitations the reciter reads, he is correct.

* *

His saying: ﴿mā hunna ummahātihim﴾ (They are not their mothers)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Their wives whom they make zihar with are not their mothers, so that they say to them, "You are to us like the back of our mothers." Rather, they are lawful to them.

* *

His saying: ﴿in ummahātuhum illā allāʼī waladnahum﴾ (Their mothers are none but those who bore them)

Meaning: none are their mothers except those who said that to them.

* *

His saying: ﴿wa innahum la-yaqūlūna munkaran mina al-qawli wa zūran﴾ (And indeed, they say an objectionable word and a falsehood)

His, the Majestic and Praised's, saying means: Indeed, the men say an objectionable word, a saying whose truth is not recognized; and zūran means falsehood, i.e., a lie.

As [Qatadah said]:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿munkaran mina al-qawli wa zūran﴾, he said: "al-zūr is al-kadhib (falsehood)." ﴿wa inna Allāha la-ʻafuwwun ghafūr﴾ means: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is possessed of pardon and forgiveness toward the sins of His servants when they repent from them and turn back, Forgiving them, so that He does not punish them for them after repentance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 3:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And those who divorce by zihar from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said - then [the penance is] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished to do, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (58:3)

His, may His praise be exalted, saying: "And those who say to their wives, 'You are to us as the back of our mothers.'"

* *

And His saying: ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "returning" (al-'awd) to what the one who made zihar said. Some of them said: it is the retracting of the prohibition that he imposed upon himself regarding his wife, who had been lawful to him before his zihar, so that he makes her lawful again after having prohibited her to himself, by resolving to have intercourse with her and to have sexual relations with her.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾, he said: "He intends to have intercourse after his saying."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾, he said: "He prohibited her, then he wishes to return to her and have intercourse with her."

Others said something similar to this view, except that they said: his keeping her after his zihar, and his not separating from her, is a return on his part to what he said, whether he resolved upon intercourse or not. Abu al-'Aliyah used to say: the meaning of His saying "li-ma qalu" ("to what they said") is "in what they said."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-'Aliyah say, regarding His saying: ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾: that is, he returns to it.

The grammarians differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of the grammarians of Basra said concerning this meaning: [the verse means] "the freeing of a slave before they touch one another; and whoever does not find [one], then fasting, then feeding sixty needy persons, then they return to what they said: 'We will not do it,' and so they do it, this zihar; he says: 'She is upon me as the back of my mother,' and what resembles this speech. So when he frees a slave, or feeds sixty needy persons, he returns to what he had said: 'She is forbidden to me,' and does it." It seems that the speaker of this view considered this to be of the inverted order (al-muqaddam alladhi ma'nahu al-ta'khir).

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾ may be rendered in Arabic as: "then they return to what they said" and "in what they said," meaning [by] "they desire marriage," i.e., "they retract what they said" and "in the annulment of what they said." He said: In Arabic it is permissible to say: "if he returns to what he did," meaning "if he does it a second time," and it is permissible: "if he returns to what he did" [to mean] "if he annuls what he did." This is like when you say: "He swore that he would strike you," meaning: "He swore that he would not strike you," and "He swore that he would surely strike you."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say that the meaning of the lam in His saying ﴿li-ma qalu﴾ is "to" (ila) or "in" (fi), because the meaning of the statement is: "then they return to annul what they said of prohibition, so that they make it lawful again." And if it is said that its meaning is: "then they return to the making lawful of what they prohibited," or "in the making lawful of what they prohibited," that is correct, because all of that is a return to it. So the interpretation of the statement is: "then they return to making lawful what they prohibited upon themselves of what Allah had made lawful for them."

* *

And His saying: ﴿then [the penance is] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another﴾

He says: upon him is the freeing of a slave, meaning the emancipation of a male or female slave, before the man who made zihar touches the wife from whom he made zihar, or she touches him.

The scholars differed regarding the intended meaning of "touching" (al-mass) in this place, similar to their difference regarding His saying: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them﴾, and we have mentioned that there.

We will mention some of what we did not mention there:

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who divorce by zihar from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said﴾: it is the man who says to his wife: "You are upon me as the back of my mother." So when he says that, it is not lawful for him to approach her, by marriage or otherwise, until he expiates his oath by freeing a slave. ﴿So whoever does not find [one], then fasting two consecutive months before they touch one another﴾, and the touching is intercourse. ﴿And whoever is not able, then feeding sixty needy persons.﴾ And if he says to her: "You are upon me as the back of my mother if I do such and such," then no zihar takes effect in that until he breaks the condition; so if he breaks it, he does not approach her until he expiates, and no divorce takes effect through zihar.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, from al-Hasan, that he did not see any harm in the one who made zihar having intercourse short of the genitals.

⁕ 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Zayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: Zihar is only from intercourse. And he did not see any harm in his satisfying his need short of the genitals, or above the genitals, or wherever he wishes, or [in] caressing.

Others said: by that is meant every sense of touching, and they said: the verse is general.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Yunus, who said: It reached me from al-Hasan that he disliked touching for the one who made zihar.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is what you are admonished to do﴾

His exalted remembrance says: your Lord has made that obligatory upon you as an admonition for you, by which you may be admonished, so that you refrain from zihar and false speech. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: His exalted remembrance says: and Allah, regarding your deeds that you do, O people, is All-Aware, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them; so refrain from speaking the reprehensible and false speech.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Then whoever cannot find [a slave], [let him fast two consecutive months before they touch each other]. And whoever is unable, [let him feed sixty needy persons]. That is so you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. And these are the limits of Allah. For the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾

His Exalted remembrance says: Whoever among you, of those who have made zihar (pronouncement of likeness) with his wife, does not find a slave to free, then upon him is fasting two consecutive months before they touch each other. The two consecutive months are those in which there is no break by breaking the fast on any day of them, except through an excuse. If the breaking of the fast is due to an excuse, there is a difference among the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) concerning it. Some of them said: if he broke his fast due to an excuse and the excuse ceased, he builds upon what has passed of the fast.

Others said: rather, he must begin anew, because whoever breaks the fast, whether with an excuse or without one, has not performed two consecutive months of fasting.

Mention of those who said: if he breaks the fast due to an excuse and the excuse ceases, he builds upon it and it is considered consecutive.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi and 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he said concerning a man who fasted for the expiation of zihar or the expiation of killing, and became ill and broke his fast, or broke it due to an excuse: "He must make up one day in place of one day, and he does not begin his fasting anew."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, the same.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib concerning the one who made zihar, upon whom is fasting two consecutive months, who fasted one month and then broke his fast: "He completes what remains."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib concerning a man who fasted one month or more of the expiation of zihar, then became ill: "He counts what has passed if he had an excuse."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us, he said: 'Umar ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, concerning a man who has a fast obligation for killing, or a vow, or zihar, who fasted part of it and then broke it: "If he had an excuse, then he makes it up."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: "If he broke it due to an excuse, he completes; and if it was without an excuse, he begins anew."

Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from 'Ata', who said: "Whoever has an obligation of two consecutive months of fasting, then becomes ill and breaks his fast, he makes up what remains upon him."

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed me, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and 'Amr ibn Dinar concerning a man who breaks his fast on a cloudy day, thinking that night had come, during the two consecutive months: "He is not required to do more than replace it, and he does not begin two other months anew."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata' who said: "If one who is in i'tikaf has intercourse while some days of his i'tikaf remain, he completes what remains; and so too the one who made zihar."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', who said: "If it is something he was afflicted with, he builds upon his fast; and if it is something he himself did, he begins anew." Sufyan said: "This is its meaning."

'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, from 'Amir concerning a man who made zihar and fasted two consecutive months except two days, then became ill: "He completes what remains."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: I heard Isma'il from al-Sha'bi with similar.

Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub narrated to us, they both said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi concerning a man who has an obligation of fasting two consecutive months, who fasted and became ill and broke his fast: "He makes it up and does not begin anew."

Mention of those who said: whoever breaks his fast, with or without an excuse, begins anew:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim concerning a man who has an obligation of fasting two consecutive months and breaks it: "He begins anew; and a woman who menstruates and breaks her fast makes it up."

Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "If he becomes ill and breaks his fast, he begins anew," meaning whoever has an obligation of two consecutive months and becomes ill and breaks his fast.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "He begins anew."

The more correct of the two opinions in our view is the opinion of the one who said: the one who breaks his fast due to an excuse builds upon it, and the one who breaks it without an excuse begins anew, because all agree that if a woman menstruates during her fast of two consecutive months, due to an excuse, the same applies to her. For the woman's breaking of the fast because of her menses is an excuse from Allah, so every excuse that comes from Allah is alike.

And His words: ﴿And whoever is unable, [let him feed sixty needy persons]﴾

His Exalted remembrance says: whoever among them is unable to fast, then upon him is feeding sixty needy persons. We have already explained the manner of feeding in the expiations earlier, so it suffices and need not be repeated.

And His words: ﴿That is so you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾

His Exalted praise says: This is what I have obligated upon the one among you who made zihar, which I did not obligate in the state of ability to free a slave; then I lightened it for him in the state of inability by fasting, and in the absence of ability to fast by feeding. I did this so that people would acknowledge the oneness of Allah and the message of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and affirm it, and act upon it, and refrain from speech of falsehood and lying. ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾: His Exalted remembrance says: these are the limits which Allah has set for you, and the obligations which He has explained for you are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them, O people. ﴿And for the disbelievers﴾ in them, who deny these limits and others, from the obligations of Allah that they be from Allah, ﴿is a painful punishment﴾: he says, a painful torment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 5:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humbled just as those before them were humbled, and We have already sent down clear signs, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, those who oppose Allah in His limits and His obligations, making limits other than His limits, that is the opposition (al-muhadda, opposing Allah and His Messenger) to Allah and His Messenger.

As for Qatadah, he used to say regarding the meaning of that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: they oppose Allah and His Messenger.

As for His saying: ﴿will be humbled just as those before them were humbled﴾, it means: they will be enraged and disgraced, just as those before them who opposed Allah and His Messenger were enraged and disgraced, and they were humiliated.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿will be humbled just as those before them were humbled﴾, he said: they will be disgraced just as those before them were disgraced.

Some of the scholars of the Arabic language used to say: the meaning of ﴿kubitu﴾ (they will be humbled) is: they will be destroyed.

Another of them said: its meaning is: they will be enraged and disgraced on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq), ﴿just as those before them were humbled﴾, meaning those who fought the prophets before them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have already sent down clear signs﴾

It means: We have already sent down distinct proofs and firm signs that point to the realities of Allah's limits.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: and for those who deny those clear signs that We sent down upon Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and reject them, is a punishment on the Day of Resurrection; humiliating means: humbling, in Hell.

The explanation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿On the day when Allah resurrects them all together, He will inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, while they have forgotten it. And Allah is Witness over all things.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment on the day when Allah resurrects them all together, and that is ﴿the day when Allah resurrects them all together﴾ from their graves to the standing of the Resurrection. ﴿Then He will inform them﴾, [that is, Allah will inform them] ﴿of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, while they have forgotten it.﴾ He, the Exalted, says: Allah has counted what they did, reckoned it against them, recorded it, and preserved it, while those who did it have forgotten it. ﴿And Allah is Witness over all things﴾ means: Allah, whose praise is great, is Witness over all things they did and over the other matters of His creation, meaning: He is a Witness who knows them and encompasses them, so nothing of them escapes Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 7:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor of fewer than that or more but that He is with them wherever they may be. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ (7)

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Have you not looked, O Muhammad, with an eye that sees, and seen ﴿that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of anything, nothing of which is hidden from Him, small or great? He, mighty is His praise, says: How then could the deeds of these disbelievers and their disobedience toward their Lord be hidden from One whose attribute is this? Then He, mighty is His praise, described His nearness to His servants, His hearing of their secret talk, and what people conceal of their conversations, when they speak privately among themselves. So He said: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three﴾ among His creatures, ﴿but that He is their fourth﴾, hearing their secrets and their private talk, and nothing of their hidden matters is concealed from Him. ﴿Nor of five but that He is their sixth﴾: He says, there is no secret conversation of five but that He is their sixth likewise. ﴿Nor of fewer than that﴾: He says, nor fewer than three, ﴿or more﴾ than five, ﴿but that He is with them﴾ when they confer privately, ﴿wherever they may be﴾: He says, in whatever place or location they are.

By His words ﴿He is their fourth﴾, the meaning is that He witnesses them by His knowledge, while He is upon His Throne.

As related:

⁕ Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad related to me, saying: Nasr ibn Maymun al-Madrub told me, saying: Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿There is no secret conversation of three﴾ ... to His words ﴿He is with them﴾, he said: He is above the Throne, and His knowledge is with them. ﴿Wherever they may be. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection﴾

His exalted remembrance says: Then He will inform these conferring persons and others of what deeds they did, of what He loves and what He abhors, on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾: He says, indeed Allah is knowing of their private talk, their secrets, the inner nature of their deeds, and other matters concerning them and His servants.

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿There is no secret conversation of three﴾. The reciters of the principal cities recited ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوَى﴾ with the letter ya (يَكُونُ), except Abu Ja'far the reciter, who recited it as ﴿مَا تَكُونُ﴾ with the letter ta (تَكُونُ). The ya is the correct reading, because the authoritative consensus upholds it, and because it is sound in Arabic.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 8:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden secret counsel, and then return to what they were forbidden, and confer together in sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you, and they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (58:8)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden secret counsel﴾ from among the Jews, ﴿then return to what they were forbidden﴾, for Allah, mighty and majestic, had forbidden them from it, ﴿and confer together in sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger﴾.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden secret counsel﴾, he said: "The Jews."

* *

His words: ﴿then return to what they were forbidden﴾

His, may His praise be exalted, says: then they return to what they were forbidden of secret counsel. ﴿And confer together in sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger﴾ — His, may His praise be exalted, says: they confer together concerning what Allah has forbidden them of abominations and enmity, which is contrary to the command of Allah, and disobedience to the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

The reciters differed in the reading of His words: ﴿wa-yatanajawna﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans and Basrans, recited it ﴿wa-yatanajawna﴾ on the pattern of yatafa'alun. Yahya, Hamzah and al-A'mash recited ﴿wa-yantajuna﴾ on the pattern of yaftaʿilun. Those who recited ﴿yatanajawna﴾ argued from His words: ﴿When you confer together (idha tanajaytum)﴾, and He did not say "idha intajaytum."

* *

His words: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And when those who were forbidden secret counsel, whose description Allah, may His praise be exalted, has mentioned, come to you, O Muhammad, they greet you with other than the greeting that Allah has made your greeting. Their greeting, with which they used to greet him, which Allah informed that He did not greet him with, as reported in the traditions, was that they would say: "As-sam 'alayka" (death be upon you).

Mention of the report transmitted concerning that:

Ibn Humayd and Ibn Waki' related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: "Some people of the Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'As-sam 'alayka, O Abu al-Qasim.' I said: 'As-sam 'alaykum, and may Allah do to you such and such.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O A'ishah, indeed Allah does not love obscenity.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you not see what they say?' He said: 'Do you not see that I return to them what they say? I say: "Upon you."' And this verse was revealed concerning that: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you, and they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾"

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: "The Jews used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: 'As-sam 'alaykum,' and he would say: 'Upon you.' A'ishah said: 'As-sam 'alaykum and the wrath of Allah.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allah does not love the obscene, the one who speaks obscenely.' She said: 'They say: As-sam 'alaykum.' He said: 'I say: Upon you.' So this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾." He said: "Indeed the Jews come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: As-sam 'alaykum."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, concerning ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾, he said: "The Jews used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: As-sam 'alaykum."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾ ... to ﴿wretched is the destination﴾, he said: "The hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they greeted him: 'Sam 'alayka.' So Allah said: ﴿Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾"

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾, he said: "They say: Sam 'alaykum." He said: "They are also Jews."

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾, he said: "The Jews used to say: Sam 'alaykum."

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that A'ishah perceived their saying, and said: "And upon you be the death and the curse." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be gentle, O A'ishah, for Allah loves gentleness in all matters." She said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you not hear what they say?" He said: "Did you not hear what I return to them? I say: Upon you."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that while the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his companions, a Jew came upon them and greeted them, and they returned his greeting. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what he said?" They said: "He said salam, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Rather, he said: sam 'alaykum, meaning, you will become weary of your religion." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did you say sam 'alaykum?" He said: "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When any of the People of the Book greet you, say: 'wa 'alayka,'" meaning: upon you is what you said.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾: "These are Jews. Three men of them came to the door of the Prophet (ﷺ) and conferred together for a while. Then one of them asked permission, and the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted him, and he said: 'As-sam 'alayka.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Upon you.' Then the second, then the third." Ibn Zayd said: "As-sam means death."

As for His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ — His, may His praise be exalted, says: those who greet you with this greeting from among the Jews say: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say to Muhammad (ﷺ), so that He hastens His punishment upon us for it?" Allah says: Sufficient for those who say this, O Muhammad, is Hell, and it suffices them to burn therein on the Day of Resurrection; and wretched is Hell as a destination.

**The exegesis of His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult privately, do not consult privately in sin and transgression and disobedience of the Messenger, but consult privately in righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾ (58:9)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿when you consult privately﴾ among yourselves, ﴿do not consult privately in sin and transgression and disobedience of the Messenger﴾, but ﴿consult privately in righteousness﴾, meaning: obedience to Allah and that which brings you near to Him, ﴿and piety﴾, that is, by guarding yourselves against Him through performing what He has obligated upon you of His duties and avoiding His acts of disobedience. ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, that is: fear Allah, to whom your final return is, and before whom you will be gathered, lest you neglect His obligations or advance toward His acts of disobedience, and He punish you for it when you return to Him.

* *

**The exegesis of His words:** ﴿Private counsel is only from Satan, to grieve those who have believed, but it cannot harm them at all, except by the permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ (58:10)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Private conversation is only from Satan. Then the scholars differed concerning the private conversation that Allah informed is from Satan, which of these it is. Some of them said: By this is meant the private conversation of the hypocrites with one another.

Mention of those who said that:

And others said: By this is meant the dreams of sleep which a person sees in his sleep and which grieve him.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Dawud al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Ata'ah was asked, while I was listening, about dreams. He said: Dreams are of three kinds. Among them is the whispering of Satan, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿Private counsel is only from Satan﴾. Among them is what a person speaks to himself about during the day and then sees at night. And among them is like a hand taking hold of him.

This is because Allah, mighty is His praise, had first forbidden it by His words: ﴿When you consult privately, do not consult privately in sin and transgression and disobedience of the Messenger﴾. Then He mentioned what is in that of harm to the people of faith, and the reason for His prohibiting them from it, saying: ﴿Private counsel is only from Satan, to grieve those who have believed﴾. Thereby He clarified [[The intended meaning of this expression is that the absence of any prior prohibition against dream-visions, and the prior prohibition against private conversation in the sense of secret discourse, both clarify what he chose, namely that najwa means secret discourse. Consider this.]], since the prohibition concerning a person's seeing in his dream was such, and it came following His prohibition of private consultation, described as being among the attributes of what He had forbidden.

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The private consultation does not harm the believers at all, except by the permission of Allah, meaning by the decree and predestination of Allah.

As for His words: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Upon Allah let the people of faith in Him rely in their affairs, and let them not be grieved by the private consultation of the hypocrites or by those who plot against them with it, for their private consultation does not harm them when their Lord protects them.

**The exegesis of His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult privately, do not consult privately in sin and transgression and disobedience of the Messenger, but consult privately in righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾ (58:9)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿when you consult privately﴾ among yourselves, ﴿do not consult privately in sin and transgression and disobedience of the Messenger﴾, but ﴿consult privately in righteousness﴾, meaning: obedience to Allah and that which brings you near to Him, ﴿and piety﴾, that is, by guarding yourselves against Him through performing what He has obligated upon you of His duties and avoiding His acts of disobedience. ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, that is: fear Allah, to whom your final return is, and before whom you will be gathered, lest you neglect His obligations or advance toward His acts of disobedience, and He punish you for it when you return to Him.
