* *

As for His words: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Upon Allah let the people of faith in Him rely in their affairs, and let them not be grieved by the private consultation of the hypocrites or by those who plot against them with it, for their private consultation does not harm them when their Lord protects them.

The Interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Make room (tafassahu) in the assemblies,' then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do."

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "O you who have believed" — that is, O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger. "When you are told, 'Make room (tafassahu) in the assemblies'" — by His saying "tafassahu," He means: make space, widen, from the phrase "makan fasih," meaning a place that is spacious.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the assembly in which Allah commanded the believers to make room. Some of them said: that was specifically the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "make room in the assemblies," he said: "The assembly of the Prophet ﷺ — that was said specifically of it."

Al-Harith related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Make room in the assemblies'..." to the end of the verse: "When they saw someone coming toward them, they would begrudge their place beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so He commanded them that some of them should make room for others."

I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: "When you are told, 'Make room in the assemblies'": "This was for the Prophet ﷺ and those around him specifically. He says: Widen [the circle] until every one of you gets a place with the Prophet ﷺ. And these are also the seats for fighting."

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "Make room in the assemblies," he said: "The people used to vie with one another for the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ, so it was said to them: 'When you are told, "Make room in the assemblies," then make room.'"

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, "When you are told, 'Make room in the assemblies,' then make room; Allah will make room for you": "This is the assembly of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. A man would come and say: 'Make room for me, may Allah have mercy on you,' and every one of them would begrudge his nearness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah commanded them to do that, and He regarded it as better for them."

Others said: rather, it refers to assemblies of fighting, when they lined up for battle.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His saying: "O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Make room in the assemblies,' then make room; Allah will make room for you": he said: "That is in the assembly of battle."

The correct view on this matter is that it should be said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded the believers to make room in the assembly, and He did not restrict that to the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ rather than the assembly of battle. Both places are called an assembly (majlis), so it applies to all assemblies, both the assemblies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the assemblies of battle.

The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the cities recited "tafassahu fi al-majalisi" in the singular, except al-Hasan al-Basri and Asim, who recited "fi al-majalisi" in the plural. The singular reading is, in our view, the correct one, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

His saying: "then make room (fafsahu)"

That is: then widen, "Allah will make room for you" — that is, Allah will widen your dwellings in Paradise. "And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up" — His remembrance, exalted is He, says: when it is said, "Arise." What is meant by that is: when it is said to you, "Stand up to fight an enemy, or to prayer, or to a good deed, or disperse from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," then stand up.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, "And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up," up to "Allah is Acquainted with what you do": he said: "When it is said, 'Rise up, then rise up,' toward good and prayer."

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "then rise up": he said: "Toward every good: fighting an enemy, or enjoining what is right, or whatever is true."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, His saying: "And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up" — he says: "When you are called to good, then respond." Al-Hasan said: "All of this is about military campaigns."

I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying "And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up": "When the call to prayer was made, some men would be sluggish, so Allah commanded them, when the call to prayer is made, to rise up toward it and stand for it."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up": he said: "Rise up from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "This concerns his house: when it is said, 'Rise up,' they should get up from the Prophet ﷺ, for he has needs, and each man among them would love for his last moment with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to be ... so He said: 'And when you are told, "Rise up," then rise up.'"

I have chosen the interpretation I have stated because Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded the believers, when they are told to rise up, to rise up, so this command encompasses all the meanings of rising up toward good things. It stands in its generality until something specific restricts it that must be accepted.

The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Madina recited "fansuzu" with a dammah on the shin, while the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited it with a kasrah.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations and established dialects, like "ya'kufun" and "ya'kifun," and "ya'rushun" and "ya'rishun." Whichever of the two readings the reciter uses is correct.

* *

His saying: "Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees"

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: Allah raises the believers among you, O people, by their obedience to their Lord in what He commanded them of making room in the assembly when they are told to make room, or by their rising up toward good things when they are told to rise up toward them. And Allah raises those among the people of faith who were given knowledge above the believers who were not given knowledge, by the excellence of their knowledge, by degrees, when they act upon what they were commanded.

As:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, His saying: "Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees": "Indeed, for the people of knowledge there is excellence, and it has a right over its people. By my life, truly there is a right upon you, O scholar, and an excellence, and Allah gives each person of excellence his excellence."

Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir used to say: "The excellence of knowledge is more beloved to me than the excellence of worship, and the best of your religion is scrupulousness."

Abdullah ibn Mutarrif used to say: "You will meet two men, one of whom fasts, prays and gives charity more, and the other is far superior to him." It was said to him: "How so?" He said: "He is the more scrupulous of the two in avoiding Allah's prohibitions."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees": "In their religion, when they do what they were commanded."

* *

His saying: "And Allah is Acquainted with what you do"

His remembrance, exalted is He, says: And Allah, O people, is fully aware of your deeds; nothing is hidden from Him of who among you obeys his Lord and who disobeys. He will recompense each of you for his deed: the one who does good with good, and the one who does evil with what he deserves, or He pardons.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 12:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [anything to give], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

His, the Exalted's, words mean: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, when you consult the Messenger of Allah privately, then let there be before your private consultation a charity which you give to the needy and the poor. ﴿That is better for you﴾ means: your giving charity before your private consultation with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better for you with Allah, ﴿and purer﴾ for your hearts from sins.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿so spend in charity before your private consultation﴾, he said: They were forbidden to consult the Prophet ﷺ until they gave charity, and none consulted him except Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who offered a dinar and gave it in charity; then the concession regarding this was revealed.

Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: al-Mutallib ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Indeed, in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, there is a verse which no one acted upon before me, and no one will act upon after me: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾. He said: It was made obligatory, then it was abrogated.

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾, he said: They were forbidden to consult the Prophet ﷺ until they gave charity, and none consulted him except Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who offered a dinar in charity and gave it away; then the concession was revealed.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Mujahid, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A verse from the Book of Allah which no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me. I had a dinar, which I exchanged for ten dirhams, and whenever I came to the Prophet ﷺ I gave one dirham in charity. Then it was abrogated, so no one acted upon it before me: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾, he said: The people questioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so much that they wearied him with questions, so Allah admonished them with this verse. A man would have a need with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ but could not fulfil it until he offered charity before him, and this was hard for them, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the concession after that: ﴿But if you do not find [anything to give], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿When you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾, he said: It was abrogated; it lasted only an hour of a day.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾ ... to ﴿indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, he said: The Muslims used to spend in charity before private consultation, and when zakat was revealed, this was abrogated.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So spend in charity before your private consultation﴾, and that is because the Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ too many questions, until they troubled him. Allah wished to lighten [the burden] on His Prophet; when He said that, many of the people were patient and refrained from asking, and then Allah revealed after this: ﴿So since you did not, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakat﴾, and Allah made it easy for them and did not constrain them.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Uthman ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ali ibn Alqamah al-Anmari, from Ali, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "What do you think? A dinar?" He said: They cannot manage it. He said: "Half a dinar?" He said: They cannot manage it. He said: "What do you think?" He said: A barley-grain. So the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Indeed, you are truly abstemious." Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Through me Allah lightened [the burden] for this Ummah. And His words: ﴿When you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾ were revealed, and then: ﴿Are you apprehensive about spending in charity before your private consultation?﴾ was revealed.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾: so that people of falsehood would not consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ privately and thereby burden the people of truth. They said: O Messenger of Allah, we cannot do that and are not able to. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Are you apprehensive about spending in charity before your private consultation? So since you did not, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakat﴾, and He said: ﴿There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for one who orders charity or what is right or reconciliation between people﴾. Whoever comes to consult you about this, accept his consultation; and whoever comes to consult you about other than this, you should cut that off from him and not consult him. He said: The hypocrites would sometimes consult privately about matters in which they had no need, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from private conspiracy, then return to what they were forbidden and conspire in sin and aggression and disobedience of the Messenger?﴾ He said: Because the wicked enter into that.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: Regarding the surah of al-Mujadilah: ﴿When you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [anything to give], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ It was abrogated by the verse after it, when He said: ﴿Are you apprehensive about spending in charity before your private consultation? So since you did not, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakat and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

* *

And His words: ﴿But if you do not find [anything to give]﴾

His, the Exalted's, words mean: But if you do not find what you can give in charity before your private consultation with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: indeed, Allah is one of pardon for your sins if you repent from them, merciful towards you in not punishing you for them after repentance, and not holding you to account for your private consultation with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before you spent in charity before your private consultation with him.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you apprehensive that you should offer charity before your private consultation? So when you do not do so and Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness], then establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

The Exalted says: Did it become difficult for you, O believers, and did you fear that you would offer charity of poverty before your private consultation with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? The original meaning of al-ishfaq (apprehension) in the speech of the Arabs is fear and caution, and its meaning in this place is: Did you fear poverty and destitution by offering charity?

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Are you apprehensive﴾: It was difficult for you to offer charity, so it was lifted from you, and they were commanded to consult the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without charity when that was difficult for them.

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Shibl ibn Abbad al-Makki, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿Are you apprehensive that you should offer charity before your private consultation? So when you do not do so and Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness], then establish prayer and give zakah﴾: They are two obligatory duties, and no one has any recourse concerning them; so this verse abrogated what had preceded it regarding the obligation of charity in private consultation.

And His saying: ﴿So when you do not do so and Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness]﴾

The Exalted says: So when you did not offer charity before your private consultation, and Allah granted you repentance for your abandoning of that, then discharge the obligations of Allah that He has made incumbent upon you and did not remove from you, namely prayer and zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger in what He commands you and what He forbids you.

﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: His praise says: And Allah is possessed of acquaintance and knowledge of your deeds, and He counts them against you in order to recompense you for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to a lie while they know [it]﴾

Almighty Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Have you not looked with the eye of your heart, O Muhammad, and seen those people who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry? They are the hypocrites (munafiqun) who have taken the Jews as allies and confidants.

As [reported]:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: They are the hypocrites who took the Jews as allies and confidants.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿have taken as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry﴾, he said: They are the Jews, whom the hypocrites took as allies.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of Almighty Allah: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry? They are neither of you nor of them﴾, he said: These are the disbelievers among the People of the Book, the Jews, and those who took them as allies are the hypocrites who took the Jews as allies. And he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿Have you not considered those who played the hypocrite, saying to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieve﴾ until ﴿And Allah testifies that they are liars﴾, [and the continuation] ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them﴾. And he said: These hypocrites said: We will not abandon our allies and associates, who will be with us for our support and might. Who will defend us? We fear that a calamity may befall us. So Almighty Allah said: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring victory or a decision from Him﴾ until ﴿in their breasts from Allah﴾. And he recited until ﴿or from behind walls﴾, and said: They do not come out.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾

Almighty Allah says: Those who took as allies these people with whom Allah has become angry are neither of you, meaning: of the people of your religion and community, nor of them, nor are they of the Jews with whom Allah has become angry. Almighty Allah described them thus as "of you" only because they are hypocrites who, when they meet the Jews, say: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they swear to a lie while they know [it]﴾

Almighty Allah says: They swear to a lie, which is their saying to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah," while they are liars, not believing in him and not having faith in him, as Almighty Allah said: ﴿Allah testifies that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾. It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man among them whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuked over a matter that had reached him about him, so he swore falsely.

Mention of the report transmitted regarding this:

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There will enter upon you a man who looks with the eye of a devil, or with the two eyes of a devil." He said: Then a blue-eyed man entered, and he said to him: "Why do you revile me or insult me?" He said: So he began to swear [oaths]. He said: Then this verse of al-Mujadilah was revealed: ﴿And they swear to a lie while they know [it]﴾, and the other verse.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 15–16:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah has prepared for these hypocrites, who took the Jews as allies, a severe punishment in the Hereafter, ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ in this world, by their deceiving the Muslims and their advising their enemies, the Jews.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they averted [others] from the way of Allah; for them is a humiliating punishment﴾

As for His saying: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, He, whose praise is great, says: They made their oaths and swearing a shield, by which they seek cover from being killed, and by which they ward off from themselves, their property, and their offspring. That is because when their hypocrisy was discovered, they swore to the believers by Allah that they were indeed among them. ﴿So they averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾: He, whose praise is great, says: they averted the believers from the way of Allah concerning them, by means of the oaths they had taken as a shield. That is because they were disbelievers, and the ruling of Allah and His way concerning those who disbelieve in Him among the People of the Book is killing or the taking of the jizyah (poll tax), and concerning the idolaters, killing. So the hypocrites averted the believers from Allah's way concerning them by their oaths that they are believers and that they are among them. Thereby they prevented the believers from killing them, and they protected themselves by it from what the people of faith in Allah would be protected from.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿for them is a humiliating punishment﴾

He says: for them is a punishment that will humiliate them in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 17:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Their wealth will not avail these hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, so that they might ransom themselves with it from the humiliating punishment of Allah, nor will their children, so that they might help them and rescue them from Allah when He punishes them. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire﴾ means: these are the ones who allied themselves with a people upon whom Allah's anger has fallen, and they are the hypocrites, the companions of the Fire, meaning its people, who ﴿abide therein eternally﴾, that is, they remain in the Fire without end.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Those whom He has mentioned are the companions of the Fire, on the Day when Allah resurrects them all. "Yawm" (the day) is connected to "companions of the Fire." By His words ﴿on the Day when Allah will resurrect them all﴾ is meant that they will be raised from their graves alive, in the same form they had before their death, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, lying and falsifying in what they say.

As evidence:

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿then they will swear to Him﴾, he said: The hypocrite will swear to Him on the Day of Resurrection just as he swore to his allies in the world.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿on the Day when Allah will resurrect them all﴾ ... the verse, and the hypocrites will swear to their Lord on the Day of Resurrection just as they swore to His allies in the world.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb al-Bakri, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was in the shade of a room, where the shade had nearly receded from him, and he said: "There will come to you a man, or there will appear a man, with the eye of a devil, so do not speak to him." He did not tarry before he came, and he looked in, and behold, it was a blue-eyed man. He said to him: "Why do you and so-and-so and so-and-so revile me?" He said: He went off and summoned his companions, and they swore that they had not done it, and so there was revealed: ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿and they think that they are upon something﴾

He says: And they suppose that in their oaths and their swearing by Allah they are upon some portion of truth, ﴿Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars﴾ in what they swear to.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verses 18–19:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The Shaytan has overpowered them, and so he has caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of the Shaytan. Indeed, the party of the Shaytan are the losers.﴾ (19)

He, the Exalted, means by His words ﴿The Shaytan has overpowered them﴾: the Shaytan has prevailed over them. ﴿And so he has caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of the Shaytan﴾: meaning his soldiers and followers. (﴿Indeed, the party of the Shaytan are the losers﴾) He says: Indeed, the soldiers and followers of the Shaytan are the ones who are destroyed, cheated in their bargain.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated﴾ (20)

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger concerning His limits (hudud) and concerning what He has enjoined upon them of His obligations, showing enmity towards Him. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: they show enmity towards Allah and His Messenger.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, similarly.

Muhammad ibn Umar narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: they show enmity, they oppose.

* *

And His saying: ﴿those are among the most humiliated﴾

He, the Exalted, says: these who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the people of humiliation (al-dhillah), because victory belongs to Allah and His Messenger.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ (21)

And His saying: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾

He says: Allah has decreed and inscribed in the Mother of the Book that I and My messengers will surely prevail over whoever opposes and defies Me.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ ... the verse, he said: Allah wrote a book and enforced it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾

He says: Indeed Allah, may His praise be exalted, possesses power and capability over everyone who opposes Him and His Messenger, so that He destroys them; He is Mighty, so no one can prevail against Him if He destroys His ally, or punishes him, or harms him in his person with evil.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 58, verse 22:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kinsfolk. Those – He has written within their hearts faith and supported them with a spirit from Him. And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah – they are the successful.﴾

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ mean: O Muhammad, you will not find a people who affirm Allah and acknowledge the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, who defy them both and go against the command and prohibition of Allah. ﴿Even if they were their fathers﴾ means: even if those who oppose Allah and His Messenger were their fathers ﴿or their sons or their brothers or their kinsfolk.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, of this verse, ﴿Have you not seen those who take as allies a people with whom Allah has become angry?﴾ [58:14], meaning they are not among the people of faith in Allah nor of the Last Day, and therefore they allied with those Jews whom they allied with.

And the people of interpretation have said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾: "You will not find, O Muhammad, a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger," meaning: those who are hostile to Allah and His Messenger.

* *

And His words: ﴿Those – He has written within their hearts faith﴾

He, the Exalted, says: those who do not love those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their kinsfolk – Allah has written faith within their hearts. What is meant by this is: He decreed faith for their hearts. The preposition "fi" here carries the sense of "li" (for), and He, the Exalted, informed that He has written faith for them in their hearts. This is because faith resides in the hearts, and since it is known from the report about the hearts that the intended meaning is their owners, mentioning the hearts suffices in place of mentioning their owners.

* *

And His words: ﴿And supported them with a spirit from Him﴾

He says: and He strengthened them with a proof from Him, and light and guidance. ﴿And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ means: and He will admit them into orchards in whose trees' beneath rivers flow. ﴿Wherein they will abide eternally﴾ means: remaining therein forever. ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ for their obedience to Him in this world, ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾ in the Hereafter, by His admitting them into Paradise. ﴿Those are the party of Allah﴾ means: those whose description is this are the soldiers and allies of Allah. ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Allah﴾ means: unquestionably, the soldiers and allies of Allah ﴿they are the successful﴾ means: they are the ones who remain and attain success by reaching what they sought, and by their pledge of allegiance in this world and their obedience to their Lord.

End of the interpretation of Surah al-Mujadila.
